text: Room settings (bridge/user/menu profiles, PIN, limits) are delivered from the database as a generated tenant dialplan context with Set(CONFBRIDGE(...)=...) lines, applied through DialplanApplyService.applyCategories which ends in a dialplan reload.

The call-center ad hoc conference (CallCenterService.addToConference, room name derived from a cleaned uniqueid, no tenant and no database row) is absorbed by the module and becomes an ephemeral room.
Rooms are either permanent or ephemeral; an ephemeral room is created from the web or from a call and expires after it ends.

Under a route mask one dialplan entry serves many rooms with different settings, so settings must be resolved at runtime, either by a CURL call back into the backend or by a per-room branch in the generated context.
The tenant room name is conf{number}_{uid}; the tenant only ever sees the short number, and internal names must never leak.
A room occupies no number in the numbering plan, but a route mask must work: route _9XX reaches room 9XX, exactly like q${EXTEN}_{uid} does for queues via normalizeTarget.
A room in a route step is only a selection among already created rooms; the mask resolves a number to an existing tenant room but must never create one on the fly.
There is no migration: no production routes with the confbridge action exist, and any stray records may be deleted.
A guest is technically an ephemeral PJSIP endpoint created per session whose context points directly at the room context, with credentials whose lifecycle is bound to the guest token.
Entry strictness is a room setting with three levels: token plus name; plus room PIN; plus moderator approval through a waiting room.
Two kinds of links exist at once: a shared room link with a TTL and revocation, and named invitations that show who entered and can be revoked individually.
Behaviour when a guest arrives before the moderator is a room setting: wait for moderator, free entry, and end the conference when the moderator leaves, mapping to wait_marked and end_marked.
Three fixed roles exist: owner, moderator, participant, mapped onto admin and marked in each participant's own ConfBridge user profile.
The owner can promote any participant to moderator, including a guest who joined through a link.
Rights live at two levels: permanent moderators stored in room settings, plus one-off grants made during a live meeting.
A tenant administrator sees and configures every room of the tenant, and entering someone else's live meeting is written to the audit log.
The available maximum is the minimum of the tariff ceiling and the live server headroom, and the tenant is never told which of the two limits applied.

Room capacity is a bandwidth budget rather than a headcount: streams grow as N times N minus one at roughly 800 kbit per second per stream, and the weight of a new participant depends on how many people are already in the room.

The tenant is shown only a number, worded exactly as 'Maximum number of participants: N'; the number is computed dynamically and may change between views, so surrounding text must not promise it is constant.
A participant over the limit is refused with an explanation: a voice announcement into the handset for phone callers and a clear error in the web client; degrading to audio-only is rejected.
Video is a mandatory part of version one, using the native ConfBridge sfu video mode with the VP8 codec.

Video reaches web participants and hardware phones, but a hardware phone sees N peers only when its max_video_streams is at least N plus one; the default is 1, so every existing endpoint is video-blind until provisioning changes it.
The layout is a grid of all participants, which requires the multi-stream sfu mode.
A single video codec is fixed by the platform and the tenant never sees this setting at all.
The live room is a full-screen page plus a mini panel reading 'you are in a conference' when the user navigates elsewhere, following the Phase 9 and 10 softphone precedent.
In the Module Hub the module first appears as a page in the base apps hub next to IVR, queues and groups; monetisation in the market hub comes later.
The guest page is a minimal shell carrying the tenant logo, without sidebar, menu or any hint of the rest of the PBX.
Mobile web is a fully functional room on a phone in version one, because a guest will most often open the link from a phone.
Recording reuses the call recording mechanics: the same records_base_path, the same access scope and Range streaming used by CDR and voicemail.
Recording starts both automatically from a room setting and from a moderator button, using the AMI ConfbridgeStartRecord and ConfbridgeStopRecord actions on the fly.
Notifying participants that recording is on is a room setting: an indicator in the web client and a voice announcement for phone participants.
Recordings are listenable both in the module, as a meeting history with a player and a participant list, and in the CDR report.
The source of room events is ConfBridge AMI events; ami.service.ts currently has no Confbridge listener at all and the queue listeners in the same file are the template.
The browser transport is SSE for events plus REST for actions.
A guest receives exactly the same event stream as an internal user; the tenant room prefix, channel names and internal identifiers are sent to nobody.
Participant states in version one are speaking now, muted, role, and video on or off; raised hand and per-channel quality are excluded.
Inviting a subscriber into a room uses AMI Originate, matching the ConfBridge engine.
Who may dial an external number, which is an outbound call spending the tenant's money, is a room setting.
Display name changes are remembered per token for a guest and only for the duration of the meeting for internal users; the subscriber card and directories are never overwritten.

The module ships a full AI adapter with read access, configuration through a diff card, and live actions such as mute and kick, plus a SKILL.md and an entry in module-coverage.registry.ts, otherwise the completeness test fails.
A conference channel that never sent BYE holds an SFU slot and starves live participants of video before max_members is reached, so the server must sweep stale channels.

The platform must maintain a static bridge profile in confbridge.conf reloaded with module reload app_confbridge.so, because video_mode cannot be set dynamically; tenant settings ride on top through Set(CONFBRIDGE(bridge,template)=...).
Client-side quality telemetry such as qualityLimitationReason, packet loss and totalFreezesDuration must be collected, because the server looks calm while the client degrades.
A custom SessionDescriptionHandler is required because stock sip.js stops the previous remote video track on every new one before the delegate is called, which would break the grid.
Joining without video happens in roughly one join in twelve and must be detected and re-negotiated.
